newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa recovers by close, funds seen.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa recovers by close, funds seen.

text.p: Cocoa futures prices rebounded from early lows to end tightly mixed on Thursday helped by late fund buying and inspired by an earlier firm trend in New York.
Traders said the renewed fund interest came as a surprise. Some saw it as technically driven.
"The fund boys decided to take it and reverse the market. I don't think it warrants an upward move and I think it should down still," said one.
Values had retraced earlier on Thursday on profit-taking and hedge selling as the market tried to consolidate recent gains.
"It's a little bit overbought and certainly the technicals suggest that we are looking for a minimum of consolidation action," said one.
Benchmark May cocoa finished at 1,006 stg a tonne, the same as Wednesday's close after profit takers drove the contract to session's low of 989 stg.
It had gained some 81 stg in a blistering rally earlier in the week but subsequently stepped back.
Activity picked up in the afternoon after a slow morning and by the close, turnover totalled 7,945 lots.
Traders cited switch activity which showed a loosening of spreads with May/July at nine stg.

Sentiment was earlier depressed by high Ivorian arrival numbers, contradicting comments by Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze who said earlier this week that the total crop would be less than one million tonnes.
According to Ivorian industry sources, arrivals at ports had already reached between 920,000 and 960,000 tonnes by March 7.
Technicallly, support is seen at a chart gap between 982 and 997 stg basis May while on the upside, resistance is pegged at Monday's peak of 1,027.
